### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/kernel.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/translation.md`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**13** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via com.acme.crm (literal, a string literal in appTranslationDataShape))_
- `content/docs/api/declarative-endpoints.mdx`  _(via com.acme.crm (literal, a string literal in appTranslationDataShape))_
- `content/docs/deployment/app-dependencies.mdx`  _(via com.acme.crm (literal, a string literal in appTranslationDataShape))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via globalActions (literal, a string literal in PlatformTranslationDataSchema; a string literal in TranslationDataSchema; a string literal in TranslationItemSchema))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via MANIFEST_ID_PATTERN (symbol, a top-level const object))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/kernel.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/translation.md`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **188** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0b539b6abbb0c30825f2f02530a3b3e96d87f106` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9073e292bc69c7a37635b13cf7854306d7035cff` — the merge of head `5877110326b041ddbfb53ac66c0d0b76acfdbc70` into base `0b539b6abbb0c30825f2f02530a3b3e96d87f106`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9073e292bc69c7a37635b13cf7854306d7035cff && git checkout 9073e292bc69c7a37635b13cf7854306d7035cff
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0b539b6abbb0c30825f2f02530a3b3e96d87f106 5877110326b041ddbfb53ac66c0d0b76acfdbc70 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0b539b6abbb0c30825f2f02530a3b3e96d87f106 && git merge --no-ff 5877110326b041ddbfb53ac66c0d0b76acfdbc70

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0b539b6abbb0c30825f2f02530a3b3e96d87f106
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0b539b6abbb0c30825f2f02530a3b3e96d87f106` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5877110326b041ddbfb53ac66c0d0b76acfdbc70`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/kernel/address-grammar.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts + packages/lint/src/i18n-walk.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-coverage.ts, ui/packages/i18n/src/useObjectLabel.ts, ui/packages/i18n/src/utils/spec-translations.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PackagesPage.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/StudioPackageSwitcher.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/TranslationPreview.tsx, packages/spec/liveness/translation.json, packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json, packages/spec/export-origins/kernel.json
Security-touching: no
Rule-change-verified: none

Read: card #35513 body and all six comments (triage 7010960754, ruling record 7125829246, re-parent 7184863702, claim 7217235557, os-dev-report 7220504764, amendment 7220537488; no earlier contract record exists), PR #37933 body, the 35-file list and the net diff against `main` (merge base `73d5e347`), and the 74 check-runs on the head. Check-runs: 74 completed, 0 pending, 0 failed; 63 success, 11 skipped (Queue verdict, Borrowed queue verdict, Dogfood Regression Gate matrix shard placeholder, Dogfood Verify CLI, 18.x upgrade harness opt-in, Packed-tarball smoke opt-in, Temporal Conformance, UI Published Artifacts, Schedule gate, and the second Auto Label / Check PR Size instances). Build Core, Type Check (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, UI), Test Core 1-10, Test UI 1-16, Spec property liveness, Check Changeset, Lint and repo gates, PR-body guards and Governed Surface Queue Guard are all success. The remainder of the diff (tests, examples, fixtures, generated references, changeset, studio namespace strings, state-counts) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT.

### ① Derived judgments

- **manifest.zod.ts +2/−28 and address-grammar.ts +34 — a pure move, right.** The 27 removed lines are the TSDoc block and the one-line declaration of `MANIFEST_ID_PATTERN`; the 34 added lines in `address-grammar.ts` are the same TSDoc (the word "here" re-pointed to `./manifest.zod.ts`, plus one new paragraph giving the reason for the home) and the same declaration. The regex literal is byte-identical on both sides: `/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*(\.[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*)+$/`. `manifest.zod.ts` now imports it beside `NAMESPACE_PATTERN` and carries `export { MANIFEST_ID_PATTERN };` at the old position.
- **Every export survives, right.** `kernel/index.ts` star-exports both `./manifest.zod` and `./address-grammar`; the two paths reach one binding, so the barrel exposes one `MANIFEST_ID_PATTERN` (no ambiguity). `api-surface/kernel.json` is untouched and still lists `MANIFEST_ID_PATTERN (const)`; `export-origins/kernel.json` changes its origin from `src/kernel/manifest.zod.ts` to `src/kernel/address-grammar.ts` and nothing else. All in-repo importers from `../kernel/manifest.zod` (`api/protocol.zod.ts`, `kernel/customization-package.ts`, `marketplace/package.zod.ts`, `manifest.test.ts`) keep resolving through the re-export. The package exports map is not in the diff.
- **Accept set of the manifest contract unchanged, right.** No line of `ManifestSchema` changes: `id` still carries `.regex(MANIFEST_ID_PATTERN, …manifestIdRefusal)`, `manifestIdRefusal` still tests the same constant, no describe text moves, no key is added, removed or tombstoned. Nothing a manifest author could write is newly refused or silently dropped. The generated kernel references carry no diff, which agrees.
- **`address-grammar.ts` "imports nothing" — true at head** (no import statement in the file), so the stated reason for the move (translation.zod.ts keys by the pattern without pulling the manifest module's graph) holds as written.
- **Translation bundle: one new accepted group, right.** `packages` enters `appTranslationDataShape()`, so it opens on `TranslationDataSchema`, `PlatformTranslationDataSchema`, `TranslationItemSchema` and (through the spread that drops only `metadataForms`) `ServedTranslationDataSchema`, hence `TranslationBundleSchema` and the `GET /i18n/translations` response. `authorable-surface/system.json` gains exactly those four rows; the generated references gain the row and the nested shape on each. Before this head a bundle carrying `packages` was refused as an unknown key on every one of those doors, so the change is a widening with no previously-accepted document now refused.
- **New refusals are confined to the new group, right.** A `packages` key that is not a manifest id is refused (`invalid_key`, with a sentence naming the rule); an unknown leaf is refused (`strictObject`); `label`, `title`, `displayName` are answered with `name`. `package` (singular) joins the alias tables of the three author doors: it was already refused as unknown there, so only the wording of an existing refusal changes.
- **Public surface outside spec, right.** `useObjectLabel()` gains `packageName` and `packageDescription` (additive); `studioSwitcherRows` gains an optional fourth parameter with a default that reproduces the old naming (`p.name || p.id`); `ExpectedEntry['source']` and `CoverageIssue['source']` gain the member `package` (a widened union: a consumer holding an exhaustive record over it has to add the key, which Type Check UI and Type Check consumer gates show is satisfied in-repo); a new diagnostic id `i18n/missing-package`.
- **No wire change on `GET /packages`, right.** The diff touches no runtime source; `manifest.name` is served as authored.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` are on the PR body and in the changeset body and match the diff: a new authorable key, nothing narrowed. The kind `added` takes at least minor on each package the diff moves, and the changeset gives minor to `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/cli`, `@object-ui/i18n` and `@object-ui/app-shell` — the five published packages whose `src` changes. `@objectstack/runtime` gains a test file only and publishes nothing. No BREAKING banner is owed: the manifest move keeps every import, and the walker's new warnings are a coverage report, not an accept-set change. Check Changeset is success on the head. Level right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Flag 1, the route change (no server overlay on `GET /packages`; the console reads the served translation document) — honours the card, not a departure from a ruled route.** The card's Expected asks for a declarable per-locale name ("for example … or a package group in the translation bundle") that package lists render for the viewer's locale with a fallback to `manifest.name`; it rules no resolution site. The two maintainer rulings on the card (7125829246 re-pointing the reach to Setup's package list and Studio's top-left; 7184863702 re-parenting under #37424) rule no route either. "Resolved server-side on GET /packages as translateApp does" is the seat's own claim line, which the same claim hands to this review, and amendment 7220537488 records the change. Judged on the tree, the client route is the sounder one: `packageActions.tsx` (line 165) states the edit path reads only the listed row's manifest, so an in-place overlay would write a translated name back as the authored one; the served document is by construction the set of groups the browser reads (`ServedTranslationDataSchema` drops only the server-resolved `metadataForms`), and `apps.APP.label` is already read there by the same hook. Acceptance against the re-pointed reach is met: Setup's list (row, group row, detail sheet title and description, search, delete-confirm) and the Studio switcher (rows and trigger) draw `packageName`, each falling back to `manifest.name` and then the id. No escalation owed.
- **Flag 3, the new `i18n/missing-package` warnings on upgrade — a correct, bounded consequence, clearable.** The walker emits `packages.ID.name` always-with-source and `.description` only when the manifest authors one (`pushOptional`), once per distinct manifest id, so the bound is at most two keys per package per declared non-default locale. The default locale is satisfied by the manifest's own text. Every emitted key is authorable: `ManifestSchema.id` enforces the same pattern the group keys by, so no valid manifest yields a key the bundle refuses. One row per package per locale clears it and `os i18n extract` scaffolds it. It is the same regime every walked group lives under (the `mappings` precedent), and `check:i18n-walk-parity` requires an emitter for a declared group. See N3 for the changeset wording.
- **open_questions 1 (should `os validate` check `packages.KEY` against the stack's known manifest ids) — answered: option A, a follow-up card.** The key grammar at parse stops a namespace or a display name but not a typo in a well-formed id, which is accepted and never renders; `validate-translation-references.ts` already collects the artifact's manifest ids, so the check has a home. Not owed in this PR: no declared behaviour is false without it.
- **out_of_scope_findings — accepted as follow-ups.** `skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md`, `content/docs/ui/translations.mdx` and `content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx` do not yet list the group; the claim excludes `skills/**`, the PR declares `Skills-docs: follow-up owed`, and the PR-body guards accept it. The seat cards both after this record, as the amendment says.
- **SQL push-down:** no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join is added on any face; the only new reads are property lookups on an already-served document. Nothing to find.
- **Security:** no `hits` path is under `skills/**` or `ui/skills/**`, and no changed hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token or authentication behaviour. Any bundle may carry a row for any package id, exactly as any bundle may already translate any app label; it is display copy only.
- **Rule change:** no `.claude/**` path is in the diff and the PR body declares none.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**`packages/spec/src/kernel/address-grammar.ts`** — holds. The constant sits beside `NAMESPACE_PATTERN`, the TSDoc's contrast between the two grammars (underscore admitted in a namespace, refused in an id) is true of both literals, and the "imports nothing" sentence is true. First consumer of the new home is `translation.zod.ts`, which imports from here and not from the manifest module.

**`packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest.zod.ts`** — holds; see ①. Tried to break it through the barrel (duplicate star export), the importers, the origin ledger and the id refusal: none moves.

**`packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts`** — holds against the card and its first consumer.
- Keyed by `manifest.id`, checked by the manifest's own grammar: the HotCRM scenario (seven packages, six apps, `revenue` with no app) needs a name per package independent of any app, and the id is what every list row carries. Every legal manifest id is a legal key, and `.custom` pair ids match too.
- Strictness: the row is a `strictObject` closed at `name` and `description`, both optional strings, with the three leaf aliases; the spec test pins the four doors plus the bundle, the single-key reading of a dotted id, the key refusal, the closed leaf and the aliases, and Test Core is green.
- Declared-is-enforced: both leaves have a live reader in this diff (`packageName` in the Setup list, the detail sheet and the switcher; `packageDescription` in the detail sheet), and the runtime pin shows the served document carrying `packages[ID]` through the real dispatcher, enabled and disabled.
- The TSDoc sentences agree with the tree: "stays the authored value on every wire" (no runtime change), "a client reads the row by direct property access" (`packageAttr`), "the served document merges every package's rows into one tree".

**Implementing files, against the contract:**
- `ui/packages/i18n/src/useObjectLabel.ts` — agrees. `packageAttr` reads `bundle[ns].packages[id][attr]` by property access across `i18n.languages`, never through a dotted `t()` key; a miss returns undefined and `packageName` falls back to `name`, then `id`; `packageDescription` to the manifest's, then undefined. Fallback when a locale lacks the row: the manifest name, as the card asks. The discovery clause adding `packages` lets a bundle that carries only this group be found; no built-in top-level key carries a `packages` child, so nothing is mis-discovered.
- `ui/packages/i18n/src/utils/spec-translations.ts` — agrees: the group is listed, so a payload carrying it alone takes the transform branch and lands under `app`.
- `PackagesPage.tsx` — agrees. Drawing and search use the shown name; search also matches the manifest name; the delete-confirm title, prompt, placeholder and arming comparison all use the one `displayName`, so the typed name always equals the one shown. The edit and view dialogs still read the manifest.
- `StudioPackageSwitcher.tsx` — agrees with ADR-0084 amendment item 2 as its header restates it: an app-carrying package keeps the app label, an app-less one takes `packageName`; the default namer reproduces the old behaviour for callers that pass none.
- `TranslationPreview.tsx` — agrees: one category row, forced by the exhaustive `satisfies` table.
- `packages/lint/src/i18n-walk.ts` and `packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-coverage.ts` — agree: paths are arrays, so the dotted id stays one segment through coverage lookup and extract; the de-duplication by id matches the comment (a composed stack restates one manifest twice).
- `packages/spec/liveness/translation.json` — the group and both leaves are `live` with evidence naming the readers above, each of which exists at head; Spec property liveness is success.

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract; left as accepted deviations or follow-ups, not to be fixed on this head):
- N1 (nit) — `manifest.zod.ts`: the long `ManifestSchema` TSDoc block (ending in the `@example App Package`) was already detached from the schema on `main`, sitting above the pattern's own doc; it now sits directly on `export { MANIFEST_ID_PATTERN };` and reads as the re-export's documentation.
- N2 (nit) — `useObjectLabel.ts`: `packageAttr` walks the language chain but takes its namespaces from the active language's bundle only, so a fallback-language row is reachable only when the active language has at least one app namespace; the result in the other case is `manifest.name`, which is still the contract's fallback.
- N3 (nit) — changeset wording: "two new warnings per locale" is per package (a seven-package stack sees up to fourteen per locale), and under `--strict` a missing key in a non-default locale is an error like every other expected key; the consequence is stated but understated.
- N4 (nit) — `StudioPackageSwitcher.tsx`: `studioSwitcherRowMatches` matches the shown label and the id, not the manifest name, while Setup's search matches both names; and Setup's list is still ordered by `manifest.name` while drawing translated names (the PR body acknowledges the sort).
- N5 (nit) — `translation.zod.ts`: on `TranslationItemSchema` the alias `package` to `packages` also answers an author who meant `overrides.package` at the top level; and the group's TSDoc says "wherever the console lists packages" while naming the two surfaces actually wired.

Follow-ups for the seat to card (outside this diff): the `os validate` manifest-id check (open question, option A); the skills and docs rows; Studio's translation table hands the walker no manifest, so it offers no row for the package name and an administrator authors it through the item's JSON view only.

## 席位核对 — L1 ACCEPT @ `5877110326b041ddbfb53ac66c0d0b76acfdbc70`

**Verdict: ACCEPT.** The at-tier contract review 7220711808 (`PASS`, tier verified on the reviewer's transcript, `No must-fix, no should-fix.`, nits N1–N5 left as accepted deviations) is posted above on this head. It covers the three spec files and the implementing files it names; the remainder below is this L1 read.

### Read at this head

- **Shape** (`l1-face.mjs --pr 37933`): draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #35513`, no closing keyword next to another card, 35 files, +666/−68, no release path, `Clause-②: yes (widening)` · `Metadata-protocol: added` on the body and the changeset.
- **`Fixes` is right.** The card asks for a declarable per-locale package name rendered by package lists with a `manifest.name` fallback; the re-pointed reach (ruling record 7125829246) names Setup's package list and Studio's top-left. Both are wired. The route change (client read of the served bundle, not a `GET /packages` overlay) departs only from the seat's own claim line, recorded in amendment 7220537488; the record finds no ruled route crossed, and I agree: an in-place overlay would be saved back by the edit dialog.
- **`Skills-docs:`** reads `follow-up #37988` (filed by the seat; the changeset's copy of the line still reads `owed`, which does not move the head).
- **Changeset l1-face flag cleared by reading:** `@objectstack/runtime` gains only `src/package-display-name-disabled.test.ts`; its build is entry-based (`src/index.ts`, `src/compiled-plugin-manifest-file.ts`) and `files` is `dist`, README, CHANGELOG, so nothing published changes and no entry is owed.
- **Changeset sentences read in person** against the head: the four doors and the refusal of `packages` before (strict shapes on `main`); the key refused at parse with the rule named, and `package` / `label` / `title` / `displayName` answered (`translation.zod.ts`); Setup's list draws the translated name on the row, the installed-apps group row and its expand label, the detail title and description, and search matches both names (`PackagesPage.tsx`); the switcher names an app-less package by it and keeps the app label otherwise (`StudioPackageSwitcher.tsx`); `manifest.name` unchanged on the wire (no runtime source in the diff); the disabled-package sentence (runtime pin, with its ablation red/green in the body); extract and `i18n/missing-package` as a warning (`i18n-walk.ts`, `i18n-coverage.ts`); the `MANIFEST_ID_PATTERN` move with re-export. All true. Minor levels on the five moved packages match `added`.
- **Generated references** (`content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx`, `.../system/translation.mdx`): one row each from the new `describe()` text; `check:generated` is green.
- **Tests** carry real commands and counts in the body; the runtime pin has an ablation; Test Core 1–10 and Test UI 1–16 ran green on this head.
- **Checks:** 63 success, 11 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending. Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check are `success`. `mergeable_state` is `clean`.

### Accepted deviations

- N3 (record): the changeset's "two new warnings per locale" is per package for a composed stack. Release prose, left as is.
- The PR-body note that Setup's list stays sorted by `manifest.name` while drawing translated names, and N4's switcher search matching the shown label and id only. Accepted.

### Out of scope

- Skills and docs rows for the `packages` group: filed #37988.
- `os validate` checking `packages` keys against the stack's manifest ids (the dev's open question; the record answers option A): to the seat's filing gate.
- Studio's translation table hands the walker no manifest, so it offers no package-name row (record follow-up): to the seat's filing gate.

### Before landing

No governed path in the diff (`docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, workflows), and under 3000 lines: Tier H is not owed. Landing is the seat's, on this ACCEPT and the PASS above at the same head.
